group.passage:
A little over a century ago, a thirsty traveler at an American train station or school had few choices. Many public places offered a barrel of drinking water with a single tin cup [[1]] to its side, and everyone, from small children to coughing old men, drank from it in turn. Few people gave the habit a second thought. As scientists learned more about germs, however, many parents grew [[2]] of letting their children use it.
One of the most [[3]] critics of the shared cup was Samuel Crumbine, a health official in Kansas who spoke out against it in newspapers and public talks. Studies of cups used in schools seemed to [[4]] his warnings, finding them covered with germs. In 1909, Kansas became the first state to [[5]] the shared cup. Other states and many railroads soon followed its example.
The new laws were good news for Lawrence Luellen, a Boston lawyer who had [[6]] a cup made of paper that each person could use once and then throw away. With his partner, Hugh Moore, he built a machine that gave out a cup of cool water for a [[7]]. The two men hoped that travelers would gladly pay for clean water, but at first the business was a [[8]], since few customers saw why they should pay for something that had always been free.
Once shared cups disappeared from public places, demand grew quickly. After the deadly flu of 1918 made people even more careful about sharing, the paper cup became a [[9]] across the country. In 1919 the partners renamed their product the Dixie Cup, after a line of dolls made by a company in the same building. Today, billions of paper cups are used every year, yet most are coated with a thin layer of plastic to stop leaks, which makes them surprisingly [[10]] to recycle.

1.explanation_zh: chain 常見的是名詞「鍊子」，這裡轉作動詞「用鍊子拴住」，chained to its side 是過去分詞片語，修飾 cup：杯子用鍊子拴在水桶邊。同一句後半說每個人都輪流（in turn）用它喝水，可見這是固定在桶邊、大家共用的同一個杯子。
evidence: Many public places offered a barrel of drinking water with a single tin cup [[1]] to its side, and everyone, from small children to coughing old men, drank from it in turn.

option_notes_zh.F: tricky（形容詞，棘手的、不好處理的）不合：空格在 a single tin cup 之後、to its side 之前，需要修飾 cup 的過去分詞。
option_notes_zh.G: outlaw 是原形，不能放在名詞後修飾 cup；「禁止共用杯子」是後來的事，要放第 5 格。
option_notes_zh.H: gamble（名詞，冒險、沒把握的事）不合：空格在 a single tin cup 之後、to its side 之前，需要修飾 cup 的過去分詞。
option_notes_zh.I: vocal（形容詞，直言不諱的、大聲疾呼的）不合：空格在 a single tin cup 之後、to its side 之前，需要修飾 cup 的過去分詞。

translation_zh.text:
一百多年前，在美國的火車站或學校裡，口渴的旅客沒有什麼選擇。許多公共場所會擺一桶飲用水，桶邊用鍊子拴著一個錫杯，從小孩到咳嗽的老人，每個人都輪流用它喝水。很少人會多想這個習慣。然而，隨著科學家對細菌了解越多，許多家長開始對讓孩子用這個杯子心生戒備。
反對共用杯子的人當中，最敢大聲疾呼的一位是堪薩斯州的衛生官員山繆．克倫拜恩（Samuel Crumbine），他在報紙和公開演講中直言反對。針對學校杯子的研究發現杯子上布滿細菌，似乎證實了他的警告。1909 年，堪薩斯成為第一個立法禁止共用杯子的州，其他州和許多鐵路公司很快也跟進。
這些新法律對波士頓律師勞倫斯．盧倫（Lawrence Luellen）來說是好消息，他早已想出一種每個人用一次就可以丟掉的紙杯。他和合夥人休．摩爾（Hugh Moore）造了一台機器，投一分錢就能得到一杯清涼的水。兩人希望旅客會樂意花錢買乾淨的水，但一開始這門生意是一場冒險，因為很少顧客明白為什麼要為一向免費的東西付錢。
共用杯子從公共場所消失後，需求快速成長。1918 年致命的流感讓人們對共用東西更加小心，紙杯從此在全國大受歡迎。1919 年，兩人把產品改名為「Dixie 杯」，名稱取自同一棟大樓裡一家公司生產的系列娃娃。如今每年要用掉數十億個紙杯，但大多數紙杯都塗了一層薄薄的塑膠來防漏，因此回收起來出乎意料地棘手。
